key_insight: 1-acetylpiperazine (PX) dynamically couples crystallization control with interface passivation to improve lead-free tin-based perovskite solar cells.
engineering_relevance: A single additive addresses both film formation and interfacial defects, offering a route toward more efficient and stable tin-based photovoltaics.
method: PX carbonyl groups coordinate with Sn²⁺ to stabilize precursor complexes and moderate supersaturation.
Controlled crystal growth produces compact, highly crystalline films.
Annealing is proposed to transform PX into amidinium-functionalized species that passivate surface A-site vacancies.
evidence_signal: Devices reached 15.18% power conversion efficiency and retained 94.1% of initial efficiency after 500 hours of continuous illumination.
watch_item: The proposed annealing-induced molecular transformation requires further confirmation; the abstract does not specify device statistics or illumination-test conditions.
paper_title: Dynamic Molecular Transformation Mediated Crystallization Regulation and Interface Passivation in Tin Based Perovskite Solar Cells
